page: Microsoft Azure D8d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration includes 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a local 307 GB SSD, though the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier for its hardware class. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng registers at 1897.59, while multi-core performance reaches 7759.55. Geekbench scores show a single-core result of 1653.0 and a multi-core result of 6177.0. Memory bandwidth tests yield 60.04 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 41.67 GB/sec for write operations. However, a performance bottleneck is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which scores 32.04 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a 307 GB local SSD provides built-in high-speed storage without requiring additional external disk attachments, optimizing the resource-to-cost ratio for data-intensive tasks. The balanced CPU-to-memory ratio and average benchmark performance make this server suitable for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, database operations, and Redis caching, where it achieves 8.08 million SET operations per second.
